question: True or false: after inflation, American house prices roughly tripled between 1890 and 1990?
answer: False. On Robert Shiller's long index, real US home prices in 1990 were not far above their 1890 level, after a deep fall and a post-war recovery. Houses wear out and new land keeps being built on, so prices long tracked building costs. The big real gains came later, mostly after 2000.
move: Check whether a trend you trust holds across the whole record.
ask: Which belief about money do I hold only because of what happened in my own lifetime?
trap: Generalising from recent decades, when house prices outran inflation.
reference: Robert J. Shiller, Irrational Exuberance, 3rd edition, Princeton University Press, 2015
